"""
Regression tests for PR #59141: REF: Make concat not stateful.

This test ensures that the changes to the concat function maintain the correct
behavior, particularly around parameter validation and handling of edge cases.
"""

import numpy as np
import pytest

import pandas as pd
from pandas import DataFrame, Series


class TestConcatRefactor:
    """Test cases for the concat refactor that makes it not stateful."""

    def test_concat_join_parameter_validation(self):
        """Test that join parameter validation works correctly."""
        # Test valid join values
        df1 = DataFrame({"A": [1, 2]})
        df2 = DataFrame({"A": [3, 4]})
        
        # These should work
        result_outer = pd.concat([df1, df2], join="outer")
        result_inner = pd.concat([df1, df2], join="inner")
        
        # This should raise ValueError with specific message
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Only can inner.*outer.*union"):
            pd.concat([df1, df2], join="invalid")

    def test_concat_sort_parameter_validation(self):
        """Test that sort parameter validation works correctly."""
        df1 = DataFrame({"A": [1, 2]})
        df2 = DataFrame({"A": [3, 4]})
        
        # These should work
        result_bool = pd.concat([df1, df2], sort=True)
        result_bool_false = pd.concat([df1, df2], sort=False)
        
        # These should raise ValueError with specific message
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="The 'sort' keyword only accepts boolean values"):
            pd.concat([df1, df2], sort="invalid")
        
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="The 'sort' keyword only accepts boolean values"):
            pd.concat([df1, df2], sort=1)
        
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="The 'sort' keyword only accepts boolean values"):
            pd.concat([df1, df2], sort="True")

    def test_concat_scalar_input_error(self):
        """Test that scalar inputs raise appropriate TypeError."""
        # Test with scalar DataFrame
        df = DataFrame({"A": [1, 2]})
        with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="first argument must be an iterable"):
            pd.concat(df)
        
        # Test with scalar Series
        s = Series([1, 2])
        with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="first argument must be an iterable"):
            pd.concat(s)

    def test_concat_empty_list_error(self):
        """Test that empty list raises appropriate ValueError."""
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="No objects to concatenate"):
            pd.concat([])

    def test_concat_keys_and_objs_length_mismatch(self):
        """Test that keys and objs length mismatch raises appropriate error."""
        df1 = DataFrame({"A": [1, 2]})
        df2 = DataFrame({"A": [3, 4]})
        
        # This should raise ValueError when keys length doesn't match objs length
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="The length of the keys.*must match"):
            pd.concat([df1, df2], keys=["x"])

"""
Regression tests for PR #59141: REF: Make concat not stateful.

This test ensures that the changes to the concat function maintain the correct
behavior, particularly around parameter validation and handling of edge cases.
"""

import pytest

import pandas as pd
from pandas import DataFrame, Series


def test_concat_join_parameter_validation():
    """Test that join parameter validation works correctly."""
    df1 = DataFrame({"A": [1, 2]})
    df2 = DataFrame({"A": [3, 4]})
    
    # Valid join values should work
    result_outer = pd.concat([df1, df2], join="outer")
    result_inner = pd.concat([df1, df2], join="inner")
    
    # Invalid join value should raise ValueError with specific message
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Only can inner.*outer.*union"):
        pd.concat([df1, df2], join="invalid")


def test_concat_sort_parameter_validation():
    """Test that sort parameter validation works correctly."""
    df1 = DataFrame({"A": [1, 2]})
    df2 = DataFrame({"A": [3, 4]})
    
    # Valid sort values should work
    result_bool = pd.concat([df1, df2], sort=True)
    result_bool_false = pd.concat([df1, df2], sort=False)
    
    # Invalid sort values should raise ValueError with specific message
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="The 'sort' keyword only accepts boolean values"):
        pd.concat([df1, df2], sort="invalid")
    
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="The 'sort' keyword only accepts boolean values"):
        pd.concat([df1, df2], sort=1)


def test_concat_scalar_input_error():
    """Test that scalar inputs raise appropriate TypeError."""
    df = DataFrame({"A": [1, 2]})
    s = Series([1, 2])
    
    # Scalar inputs should raise TypeError
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="first argument must be an iterable"):
        pd.concat(df)
    
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="first argument must be an iterable"):
        pd.concat(s)


def test_concat_empty_list_error():
    """Test that empty list raises appropriate ValueError."""
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="No objects to concatenate"):
        pd.concat([])


def test_concat_basic_functionality_preserved():
    """Test that basic concat functionality still works correctly."""
    # Test DataFrame concatenation
    df1 = DataFrame({"A": [1, 2], "B": [3, 4]})
    df2 = DataFrame({"A": [5, 6], "B": [7, 8]})
    
    result = pd.concat([df1, df2])
    assert result.shape == (4, 2)
    
    # Test Series concatenation
    s1 = Series([1, 2])
    s2 = Series([3, 4])
    
    result = pd.concat([s1, s2])
    assert result.shape == (4,)

"""
Regression tests for PR #59141: REF: Make concat not stateful.

This test ensures that the changes to the concat function maintain the correct
behavior, particularly around parameter validation and handling of edge cases.
"""

import pytest

import pandas as pd
from pandas import DataFrame, Series


def test_concat_join_parameter_validation():
    """Test that join parameter validation works correctly."""
    df1 = DataFrame({"A": [1, 2]})
    df2 = DataFrame({"A": [3, 4]})
    
    # Valid join values should work
    result_outer = pd.concat([df1, df2], join="outer")
    result_inner = pd.concat([df1, df2], join="inner")
    
    # Invalid join value should raise ValueError with specific message
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Only can inner.*outer.*union"):
        pd.concat([df1, df2], join="invalid")


def test_concat_sort_parameter_validation():
    """Test that sort parameter validation works correctly."""
    df1 = DataFrame({"A": [1, 2]})
    df2 = DataFrame({"A": [3, 4]})
    
    # Valid sort values should work
    result_bool = pd.concat([df1, df2], sort=True)
    result_bool_false = pd.concat([df1, df2], sort=False)
    
    # Invalid sort values should raise ValueError with specific message
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="The 'sort' keyword only accepts boolean values"):
        pd.concat([df1, df2], sort="invalid")
    
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="The 'sort' keyword only accepts boolean values"):
        pd.concat([df1, df2], sort=1)


def test_concat_scalar_input_error():
    """Test that scalar inputs raise appropriate TypeError."""
    df = DataFrame({"A": [1, 2]})
    s = Series([1, 2])
    
    # Scalar inputs should raise TypeError
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="first argument must be an iterable"):
        pd.concat(df)
    
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="first argument must be an iterable"):
        pd.concat(s)


def test_concat_empty_list_error():
    """Test that empty list raises appropriate ValueError."""
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="No objects to concatenate"):
        pd.concat([])


def test_concat_basic_functionality_preserved():
    """Test that basic concat functionality still works correctly."""
    # Test DataFrame concatenation
    df1 = DataFrame({"A": [1, 2], "B": [3, 4]})
    df2 = DataFrame({"A": [5, 6], "B": [7, 8]})
    
    result = pd.concat([df1, df2])
    assert result.shape == (4, 2)
    
    # Test Series concatenation
    s1 = Series([1, 2])
    s2 = Series([3, 4])
    
    result = pd.concat([s1, s2])
    assert result.shape == (4,)


def test_concat_mixed_ndim_handling():
    """Test handling of mixed dimensional objects."""
    df = DataFrame({"A": [1, 2]})
    s = Series([3, 4], name="B")
    
    # This should work - mixing DataFrame and Series
    result = pd.concat([df, s], ignore_index=True)
    assert result.shape == (4, 2)
